summary: Ferdinand Justi was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (~1856–1859) and completed his Habilitation at Marburg (~1860–1861), where he served as professor and Rektor (1887–1888).

Ferdinand Lessing worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1905), he taught at China Medical University, Peking University, the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, Humboldt University, and the University of California, Berkeley (1938).

A linguist and Indologist, Ferdinand Sommer earned his doctorate at Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen (~1893–1896) and completed his Habilitation at Leipzig. He held professorships at Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and the University of Munich (1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Geneva, Berlin, and Leipzig (PhD), where he learned under Georg Curtius, Karl Brugmann, and August Leskien. He taught at the EPHE and the University of Geneva.
Ferdinand von Eckstein was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer (~1810–1812), became a member of the Société Asiatique (~1822–1861), and founded Le Catholique in 1826.

Ferenc Ruzsa specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (~1971–1975) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982), where he later held a post around 1990.
Fernand Meyer is a scholar in Tibetology. He held positions at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2004).
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University, where he was supervised for his doctorate by Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After studying at the National University of San Marcos, he served as a professor at the University of Buenos Aires (~1970–2000) and directed the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2017).
Filippo De Filippi was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Genoa and the University of Bologna.
Filippo Marsili is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He pursued graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and held a post at Saint Louis University (attested 2019).

Finnian M. M. Gerety works in Indology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Harvard University under Michael Witzel, held a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale (2017–2018), and became a visiting assistant professor at Brown University (attested 2020).

Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Sanskrit College, held a chair at King's College London (1862), and was librarian at the India Office.

Flavio Geisshuesler specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Bern, Lausanne, and Virginia (PhD under David Germano), and held posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2019) and the University of Sydney (~2022).
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she taught Jacques Giès.

Florin Deleanu is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Bucharest, Peking, Waseda, and Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen). His appointments include professorships at Kansai Medical University and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Florinda De Simini is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Turin. She held fellowships at IIAS and Hamburg, and became an associate professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2016).

Frances Wood is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Newnham College and Peking University, and held a post at the British Library from ~1977 to 2013.
Francesca Fremantle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1966–1971) and studied under Chögyam Trungpa (~1971–1975).

Francesco Sferra is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar who studied under Raffaele Torella. He has served as a professor and director at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and held a professorship at the University of Naples Federico II.
